## How can I help you?

**Looking to hire a Performance Marketing Manager:** 10+ years of in-house and agency-side experience managing large-scale lead gen accounts. See background and career results at /for-employers.

**Need an audit, consultation, or account management:** A clear-eyed look at what's working and what isn't in your Google, Microsoft, or Meta Ads account, or ongoing management. See /services.

## How I Work

**Start with the goal, not the tactic.** I focus on the number that actually matters, usually lowering cost per action and scaling conversion volume at the same time, not one at the expense of the other.

**Fix the foundation first.** Before touching bids or creative, I make sure tracking and data are accurate. Every scaling decision after that is only as good as the data it's built on.

**Then experiment relentlessly.** Once the foundation is solid, I test across every layer of the account, including bidding strategy, audience signals, ad copy, and landing pages, to find what actually moves the number.

# Paid Search & PPC Case Studies

Case studies drawn from real accounts I've managed. Screenshots are watermarked; client names shown only where permitted.

### Health Insurance : iHealthQuotes.com
**Context:** As Director of Marketing at P7 Ventures, led multi-channel paid search strategy for this health insurance brand across all business units.
**Platforms:** Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, other PPC platforms, vendors
**What I did:**
- Led multi-channel paid search strategy, managing vendors and hitting aggressive CPA and volume targets
- Optimized the Google Ads account and launched Microsoft Ads and other PPC platforms to diversify and scale acquisition
- Architected automated data pipelines for real-time ROI tracking and full performance transparency
**Result:** Scaled the whole lead gen program 5X in 2 years, helping the brand reach #24 on the Inc. 5000 list in 2025. Source: https://www.inc.com/profile/ihealthquotes

### Mental Health : Riverhouse Wellness (riverhousewellness.com)
**Context:** Built the entire performance marketing infrastructure for a new mental health and substance use disorder treatment brand from scratch, as part of P7 Ventures' behavioral health business unit.
**Platforms:** Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, vendors, and specialized platforms such as recovery.com
**What I did:**
- Built the entire performance marketing infrastructure, conversion tracking, and data pipelines from scratch for a new brand launch, using CallTrackingMetrics, Salesforce, and n8n
**Result:** Reached operational scale within 90 days.

### Insurance Lead Gen at Scale (Multi-Vertical)
**Context:** As Head of PPC managing insurance lead and call generation across six verticals: Medicare (O65), health (ACA and U65), life, final expense, auto, and home.
**Budget scale:** $100,000+/day
**Platforms:** Google Ads (Search, Display, Discovery, YouTube), Bing Ads, Facebook Ads, and dozens of specialized PPC platforms
**What I did:**
- Built and managed PPC campaigns across Google Ads, Bing Ads, and Facebook Ads for six insurance verticals simultaneously
- Conducted in-depth data analysis using Tableau, QlikView, Google Analytics, and Power BI
- Ran A/B and split tests to identify and act on growth opportunities
- Recruited, trained, and managed a team of PPC specialists
**Result:** Consistently hit KPI and daily budget targets across all six verticals, and scaled the health insurance vertical by 25X.

### E-commerce (Home Appliances) : E-techno
**Context:** Managed paid search for a large e-commerce catalog spanning 30,000+ items in home appliances, plus a wide range of consumer product categories including electronics, home goods, outdoor, personal care, and apparel.
**Platforms:** Paid Search
**What I did:**
- Optimized paid search accounts
- Built a Power BI analytics system from scratch, including the data model and reports used for marketing and management decisions
**Result:** Grew monthly orders by 36x and reduced cost per order by 2.5x.

## Blog : https://kseniiashermin.com/blog/

Articles on paid search and PPC, written from hands-on account management. Full posts below.

### Microsoft Ads vs Google Ads: Cost, Competition, and Bot Traffic (2026 Data) : https://kseniiashermin.com/blog/microsoft-ads-vs-google-ads/

Published September 4, 2026.

Microsoft Ads costs 25 to 40 percent less per click than Google Ads on average, mainly because far fewer advertisers bid there, and its cost per conversion runs about 31 percent lower across most industries. Google still converts at a higher rate overall and dominates on raw search volume. Neither platform wins outright: Microsoft wins on efficiency, Google wins on scale, and the platform with less competition also carries a traffic-quality risk that Google advertisers rarely have to think about.

**2026 benchmarks:** Google Ads averages $2.85-$5.26 CPC with ~80% of US advertisers running it and an ~8.18% cross-industry conversion rate. Microsoft Ads averages $1.50-$2.80 CPC (25-40% lower, wider in B2B and legal) with ~36% of US advertisers running it and a ~3.5% cross-industry conversion rate, though top verticals (careers, finance, real estate) reach 5-7%. Microsoft's cost per conversion runs about 31% lower than Google's on average. Google Ads' per-campaign IP exclusion limit is 500; Microsoft Ads' is 100, campaign level only.

**Why Microsoft is cheaper:** fewer advertisers bidding means a thinner, less competitive auction, not a smarter algorithm.

**The catch:** an estimated 8.51% of all paid ad traffic industry-wide is invalid in 2026, reaching up to 40% in high-cost verticals like finance, insurance, legal, and home services. Microsoft doesn't publish its own invalid-traffic rate, but its smaller advertiser base means bad placements get flagged more slowly than on Google, and the Syndicated Search Partners network is a common source of high-click, low-conversion traffic.

**How to keep a Microsoft Ads account clean:** pull the Website URL (Publisher) report weekly, maintain a shared negative site list at the manager account level, review search terms weekly, and test restricting delivery to Bing and Yahoo (owned and operated) only versus the default syndicated network.

**Real account example:** in one national US services account, Google Ads averages $9.20 CPC at 5.5% conversion (~$167 cost per conversion) versus Microsoft Ads at $2.64 CPC and 2.21% conversion (~$119 cost per conversion, about 29% lower than Google despite converting at less than half the rate).

FAQ covers: whether Microsoft Ads is cheaper than Google Ads, whether it converts as well, whether its cost per conversion is lower, whether it has a bot traffic problem, how often to update the negative site list, and whether every advertiser should run both platforms.

Full article, benchmark table, and sources at the URL above.

## Work With Me (Services) : https://kseniiashermin.com/services/

# Work With Me

Lead generation focused paid search and paid social, for B2C, B2B, and service businesses.

## Audit
A full review of your Google Ads and/or Microsoft Ads account, including structure, settings, conversion tracking, budget allocation, and bidding strategy. You receive a written report covering the findings, a recommended improvement strategy, and a prioritized list of what to fix first.

Access to the advertising account is required. Implementation is discussed separately, depending on the audit findings and scope of work.

## Consultation
A focused strategy session. Bring your specific questions or roadblocks, leave with a concrete plan.

## Account Management
Ongoing, hands-on management of your Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and/or Meta Ads accounts, built around a predictable lead pipeline.

## FAQ

**What's included in a paid search audit?**
A full review of your Google Ads and/or Microsoft Ads account, including structure, settings, conversion tracking, budget allocation, and bidding strategy. You receive a written report covering the findings, a recommended improvement strategy, and a prioritized list of what to fix first.

**What access do you need for an audit?**
I need access to the advertising account to review its structure, settings, tracking, and performance.

**Does the audit include implementation?**
Implementation is discussed separately, depending on the audit findings and the scope of the work needed.

**Do you work with e-commerce accounts?**
Yes, I have experience with large appliance e-commerce (30,000+ items) and I've worked across a wide range of consumer product categories, from electronics and home goods to outdoor, personal care, and apparel.

**Which platforms do you work with?**
Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn Ads, and other PPC platforms depending on where your audience is.

**Which industries have you worked in?**
Health insurance (ACA, U65, and Medicare O65), life and final expense insurance, auto and home insurance, mental health and behavioral health treatment, telecom and internet service providers, e-commerce, including home appliances and consumer goods, and B2B SaaS.

**Do you sign NDAs?**
Yes, if needed.
